data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word Γαλλικός (Gallikos), meaning 'Gallic' or 'of Gaul'. The name may have also referred to a servant girl in ancient Greece. In the New Testament, Galatians was the name of a province in Asia Minor and the people who lived there. The name Gal carries the meaning “Gallic, foreigner, or servant girl” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gal usually hope their child will grow to embody gallic, foreigner, or servant girl and live with faith, good character and purpose.
